title.narrative: The resilience of the Kenyan horticultural sectors enabling environment (competent authorities and support services) is improved in order to strengthen the competitiveness of the Kenyan origin, by means of, among others, enhanced SPS compliance

description.narrative: The enabling environment of the Kenyan horticultural sector targeted by the programme is constituted of support services, competent authorities and public/private national task forces. Specific activities will include:2.1.Design and implement individual support projects for competent authorities.2.2.Design and implement individual support projects for support services. This includes tailored and collective support for individual beneficiaries (public and private organisations) involved in the strengthening of the Kenyan horticultural industrys competitiveness (consultants, research organisations, training centres, universities).2.3.Develop, adapt and disseminate existing training modules to cover plant health and SPS troubleshooting, with a focus on high priority health and trade concerns.2.4.Develop, adapt and implement SPS good practice guides following the process developed under previous and current COLEACPmanaged programmes in coherence with EU and nonEU funded previous and current programmes, where practicable.2.5.Support the testing of smart and innovative technologies for sustainable production and trade to improve the competitiveness of the Kenyan horticultural industry. This includes, among others, greenhouse design, irrigation techniques, postharvest handling, pest monitoring and surveillance, logistics, value addition, improved traceability for complex supply chains involving outgrowers.

Specific activities will include:2.1.Design and implement individual support projects for competent authorities.2.2.Design and implement individual support projects for support services. This includes tailored and collective support for individual beneficiaries (public and private organisations) involved in the strengthening of the Kenyan horticultural industrys competitiveness (consultants, research organisations, training centres, universities).2.3.Develop, adapt and disseminate existing training modules to cover plant health and SPS troubleshooting, with a focus on high priority health and trade concerns.2.4.Develop, adapt and implement SPS good practice guides following the process developed under previous and current COLEACPmanaged programmes in coherence with EU and nonEU funded previous and current programmes, where practicable.2.5.Support the testing of smart and innovative technologies for sustainable production and trade to improve the competitiveness of the Kenyan horticultural industry. This includes, among others, greenhouse design, irrigation techniques, postharvest handling, pest monitoring and surveillance, logistics, value addition, improved traceability for complex supply chains involving outgrowers.

title.narrative: The capacities of agribusinesses and exporters associations in the Kenyan horticultural sector to compete on domestic, regional and international markets are reinforced

description.narrative: This result aims target operators and business membership organisations. Activities are designed around COLEACPs Sustainability Framework. This provides a simple framework for continuous improvement, focusing on the business case so that adopting good practice not only facilitates market access, but genuinely helps suppliers run more efficient, profitable and resilient businesses. Specific activities include the following:1.1.Design and implement individual support projects with target operators, with tailored and collective support for individual beneficiaries (training courses, coaching to put new skills into practice, advice and technical assistance). 1.2.Design and implement individual support projects with business membership organisations, with tailored and collective support for individual beneficiaries (training courses, coaching to put new skills into practice, meetings facilitation, advice and technical assistance).1.3.Develop, adapt and disseminate training materials, technological innovations, crop production protocols, crop protection guides, good practices guides, technical bulletins and website advisory databases, in line with evolving SPS, plant health, commercial, social and environmental requirements, ensuring thereby safe food for consumers on all markets while improving the competitiveness and preserving the environment.1.4.Facilitate access to finance for target operators, in particular through close collaboration and partnership with specialised access to finance support structures and organisations

description.narrative: This result aims target operators and business membership organisations. Activities are designed around COLEACPs Sustainability Framework. This provides a simple framework for continuous improvement, focusing on the business case so that adopting good practice not only facilitates market access, but genuinely helps suppliers run more efficient, profitable and resilient businesses. Specific activities include the following:1.1.Design and implement individual support projects with target operators, with tailored and collective support for individual beneficiaries (training courses, coaching to put new skills into practice, advice and technical assistance). 1.2.Design and implement individual support projects with business membership organisations, with tailored and collective support for individual beneficiaries (training courses, coaching to put new skills into practice, meetings facilitation, advice and technical assistance).1.3.Develop, adapt and disseminate training materials, technological innovations, crop production protocols, crop protection guides, good practices guides, technical bulletins and website advisory databases, in line with evolving SPS, plant health, commercial, social and environmental requirements, ensuring thereby safe food for consumers on all markets while improving the competitiveness and preserving the environment.1.4.Facilitate access to finance for target operators, in particular through close collaboration and partnership with specialised access to finance support structures and organisations

title.narrative: Bottlenecks affecting the competitiveness of Kenyan agricultural exports are assessed and addressed through enhanced policy dialogue

description.narrative: This result will focus on identifying and monitoring decisions, policies and trends that have a potential impact on competitiveness and market access for Kenyan suppliers. This will cover amongst other regulations (food safety, plant health, environment, organic); the donor environment (development programmes and practitioners); and the business and commercial environment. The latter will address international standards, regulations, private standards, buyer practices, competing origins, international transport and cargo logistics (in terms of cost, frequency and quality of the service, transit times and tax regimes on county and national level). Specific activities will include the following:3.1.Design and implement individual support projects with other stakeholders of the Kenyan horticultural sector 3.2.Perform a diagnosis study of bottlenecks affecting the competitiveness of the Kenyan horticultural exports.3.3.Design and implement a series of pilots / proofofconcepts / feasibility studies in order to assess and evaluate the viability of the proposed policy solutions prior to their upscaling through evidencebased analyses.3.4.Facilitate the establishment and implementation of active and effective national publicprivate dialogue to tackle challenges and bottlenecks impairing the competitiveness of the Kenyan horticultural exports and defend the interests of the Kenyan horticultural sector when represented at national, regional and international level.3.5.Participation in public, private and donor committees/forums and technical working groups that discuss and address issues and bottlenecks impairing the competitiveness of the Kenyan horticultural sector, including but not limited to EU pesticide maximum residue levels (MRLs), EU plant health regulations, organic regulations, enforcement of standards, and measures towards better functioning of the food valuechain. 3.6.Participation in national, regional and international trade fairs to meet with existing and potential buyers as well as exploratory commercial missions to open new markets, trade negotiations/economic forums, where Kenyan interests are defended and to ensure the Kenyan origin is promoted.
